author: Great Lakes Wire
title: Moolenaar and Cline introduce bill to bar entry, deport PLA-linked company employees
text:
Moolenaar and Cline introduce bill to bar entry, deport PLA-linked company employees
Congressmen John Moolenaar and Ben Cline introduced the No PLA Employees Act on June 10. The proposed legislation would prohibit current and former employees of companies identified by the Department of Defense as supporting China's People's Liberation Army or engaging in problematic activity from being admitted into the United States. It would also permit deportation of such individuals currently residing in the country.
"The Chinese Communist Party is working tirelessly to make the PLA the world's leading military force by 2050. Through its policy of civil-military fusion, it has enlisted dozens of companies, and their subsidiaries, to assist in that goal. Beyond that, the CCP expects any Chinese national abroad to support its cause if called upon. Our commonsense legislation ensures that those who have already worked to advance the CCP's mission are not permitted in the United States, while protecting Chinese immigrants who seek to flee the regime's persecution," said Moolenaar.
Cline said, "At a time when the Chinese Communist Party is working aggressively to expand its influence over the United States economy and technological advancements, we cannot afford to hand over critical research and jobs to entities with ties to our greatest adversary. I am proud to work with Rep. Moolenaar to restrict visas to companies and employees with CCP links, ensuring hostile nations do not have access to our innovation, intellectual property, or critical infrastructure and strengthening America’s workforce and national security."
Moolenaar serves as Chairman of the House Select Committee on China. Cline is a member of the House Committee on the Judiciary, which oversees immigration policy.
John Moolenaar has represented Michigan’s 2nd district in Congress since 2015 after previously serving in both chambers of Michigan’s legislature; he was born in Midland in 1961 and graduated from Hope College with a Bachelor of Science degree in 1983, according to his official congressional biography.
